claims.text: DFT+DMFT accurately captures local, dynamical electron correlations in itinerant magnetic systems.
Local, dynamical electron correlations are responsible for ferromagnetic ground states in itinerant magnetic systems.
DFT+DMFT can be applied using optimized on-site Coulomb interaction, Hund's coupling, and double-counting parameters.
Quantum many-body effects dominate under the stated zero-temperature ground-state conditions.
On-site Coulomb repulsion and Hund's coupling generate local electron correlations.
Local electron correlations modulate exchange interactions.
DFT+DMFT captures dynamical electron-correlation effects beyond static mean-field approximations.
Capturing dynamical correlations improves the balance between kinetic energy and exchange interactions.
The balance between kinetic energy and exchange interactions is critical for accurately predicting ferromagnetic ordering.
DFT+DMFT should improve prediction of a ferromagnetic ground state relative to standard DFT or DFT+U.
DFT+DMFT should produce magnetic moments and magnetic-state energy differences that more closely match experiment than standard DFT or DFT+U.
Standard DFT or DFT+U may underrepresent or mispredict ferromagnetic ordering because they treat many-body dynamical correlations insufficiently.
DFT+DMFT accuracy may degrade when non-local correlations are significant.
Inaccurate choices of U, J, or the double-counting correction may degrade DFT+DMFT predictions.
Quantitative DFT+DMFT predictions depend heavily on U, J, and the double-counting correction.
